    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Victoria ← Latin victoria ← victor ← vincere (to conquer)",
    "reading": "conquest, triumph, the act or state of victorious overcoming",
    "languages": ["la","en"],
    "source": "Oxford Latin Dictionary; Lewis & Short",
    "confidence": 0.95
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Vic-tor-ia → Vic (French: saw, as in tool) + tor (French: bull, toro) + ia",
    "reading": "the saw of the bull; cutting power of the masculine force",
    "languages": ["fr","en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.65
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Victoire (French homophone) → vis (force) +toire (twists, from tordre)",
    "reading": "twisting force; the spiral power that conquers",
    "languages": ["fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.7
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Victoria ≈ Victoire ≈ Victoire (Fr) ≈ victoire (Fr: victory) ≈ vika (Skr: to separate, to divide)",
    "reading": "the dividing victory that separates winner from loser",
    "languages": ["fr","sa"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.55
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "VICTORIA → I, VICTOR → I, VICTORY",
    "reading": "the self-declared victor; ego claims the palm",
    "languages": ["en","la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Vic-to-ria → Vic (Old French: alive, from Latin vivus) + to-ria (tore, torn)",
    "reading": "the living torn apart; life rent by victory",
    "languages": ["fr","la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "V.I.C.T.O.R.I.A. → Vivit In Carne, Tamen Occidit Regnum Inimici Animæ",
    "reading": "lives in flesh yet slays the kingdom of the enemy of the soul",
    "languages": ["la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "V (hook, nail, victory sign) + I (axis, one) + C (crescent, moon) + TOR (bull) + IA (goddess suffix)",
    "reading": "the nailed axis of the lunar bull-goddess; fixation of cyclic power",
    "languages": ["en","la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.45
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Victoria ≈ Viktoria (Ger) ≈ vikt (Swedish: weight) + oria (aura, golden light)",
    "reading": "weight of golden light; heavy glory that conquers",
    "languages": ["sv","la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Victoria ← *weik- (Proto-Indo-European: to fight, to conquer)",
    "reading": "the embodied force of combat and decisive overcoming",
    "languages": ["ine","la","en"],
    "source": "Pokorny, Indogermanisches etymologisches Wörterbuch",
    "confidence": 0.85
  }
]
